title: PES 0110 writes a stitch pattern as a CEmbOne stitch group
description: design.export with pesVersion 11 writes an imported stitch pattern as a CEmbOne object with its CSewSeg runs, as PE-DESIGN 11.50 writes the stitch group of a version 6 file it re-saves (compat/reference/pes/pes-csewseg-trims.pes, pes-default-v6.pes, pes-design-properties.pes). The source is PE-DESIGN's re-save of pes-csewseg-trims: two Red running lines (20,20)-(60,20) and (20,60)-(60,60) mm with a trim between them.

evidence.note: docs/FILE_FORMATS.md, PES 0110 object list, CEmbOne: mapped from PE-DESIGN 11.50's re-saves of three version 6 files; the writer's rewrite of those files is byte-identical outside the documented differences (pes11.rs, written_object_sections_match_pe_designs_bytes_outside_the_documented_differences)

references.make: Run `stitchtool compat --only pes-0110-stitches` and open target/compat/work/pes-0110-stitches/a.pes in PE-DESIGN 11 (App menu > Open). Expected: two Red running lines (20,20)-(60,20) and (20,60)-(60,60) mm as one stitch pattern (a grouped stitch object, as PE-DESIGN shows a version 6 file), one colour, the move between the lines drawn as a jump, 40.00 x 40.00 mm. Record in the MANIFEST notes: whether the file opens and with what warning, whether the object is a stitch pattern that can be selected and moved, the colour shown in Sewing Order (800 RED expected), and the status-bar size and stitch count. Then Save As PES, default type (Layout & Editing Ver.11.0 File, #PES0110), unchanged, under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md). If PE-DESIGN refuses the file or opens it blank, do not add a file: write what you saw in the notes of docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md instead.
